description: KARUNX LABS is a research-driven initiative working at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Computational Biology. We focus on developing computational methods and intelligent systems for challenges in biology, healthcare, and space science.
summary: HELIX is a computational systems biology platform developed by KARUNX LABS that models spaceflight-associated human immune dysregulation across molecular and physiological scales. Spaceflight exposes astronauts to microgravity, ionizing radiation, and physiological stress that disrupt T-cell activation, Natural Killer (NK) cell cytotoxicity, and inflammatory cytokine signaling (IL-6/NF-κB), while small astronaut cohort sizes (N = 4–12) cause purely black-box machine learning models to overfit. HELIX solves this by integrating verified human spaceflight cohorts from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSD-570, OSD-575, OSD-569, OSD-53) with coupled ordinary differential equation (ODE) immune kinetics and group-validated hybrid residual machine learning (Y_hybrid = Y_mechanistic + f_θ). Through an interactive mission-control web interface, researchers and mission planners can simulate immune recovery trajectories, quantify biomarker shifts under variable mission durations and radiation doses, and evaluate countermeasure scenarios with explicit data provenance and 95% confidence bounds.
details:
What Does HELIX Do & How Does It Work?

HELIX is a space biology intelligence platform built by KARUNX LABS to simulate, quantify, and interpret spaceflight-associated human immune dysregulation across molecular and physiological scales. It operates through a multi-stage computational pipeline:

1. NASA OSDR Data Ingestion & Provenance Engine: Queries and harmonizes human spaceflight transcriptomic and immune cohorts from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSD-570, OSD-575, OSD-569, OSD-53), aggregating gene-level signals into biologically grounded immune pathways (including IL6, NFKBIA, IL2RA, GZMB, PRF1, and IFNG) with explicit data-provenance badges.

2. Coupled Mechanistic Immune ODE Solver: Uses SciPy's RK45 differential equation solver to simulate baseline T-cell TCR/IL-2 activation, Natural Killer (NK) cell cytolytic activity, and pro-inflammatory cytokine kinetics under mission duration, microgravity, and ionizing radiation stress.

3. Subject-Blocked Hybrid Residual Machine Learning: Rather than relying on black-box ML that overfits small astronaut cohorts (N = 4–12), HELIX predicts residual biological variance on top of the mechanistic ODE baseline (Y_hybrid = Y_mechanistic + f_θ) using regularized ElasticNet and shallow XGBoost models validated via zero-leakage GroupKFold cross-validation and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.

4. Interactive Mission-Control Interface: Exposes real-time biomarker trajectory simulations, radiation/stress sensitivity sweeps, and model ablation benchmarks in a dark "Liquid Glass" web interface.

Benefits & Intended Impact

- Prevents Small-Cohort Overfitting: Anchoring machine learning residuals to mechanistic ordinary differential equations preserves physiological plausibility even with limited astronaut sample sizes.

- Actionable Mission Risk Assessment: Enables spaceflight researchers and mission planners to evaluate immune suppression, inflammatory spikes, and post-flight recovery windows for long-duration LEO, lunar, and Mars missions.

- Open & Reproducible Science: Every output carries explicit provenance metadata and open-source code so researchers can audit model assumptions and extend datasets.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

- Backend & Scientific Computing: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, NumPy, SciPy (RK45 ODE integration), Scikit-learn (ElasticNet, GroupKFold), and XGBoost.

- Frontend & Deployment: Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, GitHub Actions CI/CD, and GitHub Pages.

- Data Sources: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) / GeneLab APIs.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

- Hybrid Physics-Informed Biology: Combines first-principles systems immunology equations with residual machine learning instead of treating spaceflight omics as a purely statistical problem.

- Zero-Leakage Validation & Transparency: Strictly groups cross-validation splits by subject/mission cohort to prevent data leakage and displays clear provenance indicators so users always know which values derive from NASA OSDR empirical cohorts versus mechanistic-hybrid simulations.
